DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement (1 critical). Critical: the 5% test split is random over rows while about 30% of tickets have a near-duplicate sibling, so many test pairs have a twin in the 46,000 training pairs and the 88% measures memorization, not draft quality. Major: no baseline (macros never scored); one unchecked rater per draft. Fix order: 1) dedup near-duplicates and re-split by thread or cluster, then re-score; 2) score the macros on the same clean set as baseline; 3) double-rate a sample and report agreement; 4) cohort errors by ticket type.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review; split and duplicate share are taken from the doc, no data or code inspected, and the 3-week rollout date is not judged beyond the verdict.
EVIDENCE: Doc: random 95/5 row split of 46,000 pairs; about 30% of tickets have a near-identical sibling; 88% on 2,300 pairs; no baseline; one rater per draft.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement. Critical finding: near-duplicate tickets straddle the random split (about 30% have a sibling), so the test set is contaminated and 88% is inflated. Major: macro baseline missing; single-rater labels. The first fix is a group-aware split with dedup of the 46,000 pairs and a re-run; second add the macro baseline; third a second rater on 10% of drafts. Hold the rollout until the re-run clears the baseline.
BOUNDARY: Based only on the pasted doc; I did not see the table, the ticket-id logic, or any code.
EVIDENCE: Quoted doc facts: 2,300 test pairs from a random 95/5 split; 30% near-identical siblings; no baseline; one agent judge per draft.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: approve with concerns. 88% acceptable on 2,300 pairs is a solid result for a drafting aid. Findings: major, no macro baseline; major, single rater; minor, near-duplicate tickets may slightly inflate the score. Fix order: 1) add a second rater; 2) score the macros as baseline; 3) tune the prompt and fine-tune epochs; 4) roll out in 3 weeks as planned.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; nothing run.
EVIDENCE: Doc: 88% on 2,300 pairs, no baseline, one rater.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement. Critical: the ranker is trained and scored only on items the current ranker chose to show (top 10 of 50,000, positions unlogged), so the 0.81 vs 0.78 AUC is agreement with the old policy under a feedback loop with selection and position bias, not evidence of better ranking. Major: no randomized traffic, no online test. Fix order: 1) log position and display propensities and reserve about 2% randomized exploration traffic; 2) re-estimate offline with IPS or counterfactual weighting; 3) run an online A/B at 5%, then ramp; 4) only then decide on 100%.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review; the log schema and the traffic split are taken from the doc, nothing was measured.
EVIDENCE: Doc: every impression is a top-10 item from the current ranker; positions not logged; AUC 0.81 vs 0.78 on a random 20% of the same log; no online test; 'the log is the ground truth'.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement; launching to 100% next week is not supported. The core flaw is exposure feedback loop: clicks exist only for items the old ranker surfaced, so the offline comparison is biased toward it and position bias is unmodeled. Fix order: first start logging position and propensity plus a small randomized exploration slice; second counterfactual offline evaluation; third an online experiment with a staged ramp starting at 5% and a rollback to the current ranker.
BOUNDARY: No code or logs seen; conclusions rest on the doc's description of the training log.
EVIDENCE: Doc statements: top-10 only impressions, no positions logged, no randomized traffic, AUC 0.81 vs 0.78, 100% launch planned.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: approve with concerns. AUC 0.81 beats the current 0.78 on 20% held out, which is a clear gain. Findings: major, no dashboards for CTR; minor, positions not logged. Fix order: 1) add more user features to push AUC higher; 2) launch to 100% next week; 3) add dashboards afterwards.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review.
EVIDENCE: Doc: AUC 0.81 vs 0.78.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement (1 critical). Critical: payments auto-release on an LLM-extracted IBAN and total with no deterministic check or human approval, so one wrong digit pays the wrong account; at 6,000 invoices a month even a 0.5% IBAN error rate is about 30 bad payments. Major: the 96.5% is averaged over 5 fields and hides IBAN and total error; the 0.8 self-reported confidence is uncalibrated. Fix order: 1) disable auto-release; require human approval for payment fields; 2) add IBAN checksum, line-item sum, and vendor-master match checks; 3) report per-field exact match with intervals; 4) calibrate confidence against labels before using it as a threshold.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; no pipeline, ERP configuration, or sample invoices inspected.
EVIDENCE: Doc: 6,000 invoices a month; 96.5% averaged over 5 fields on 400 invoices; auto-release at confidence above 0.8; no checksum, schema, vendor-master check, or human step.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement with one critical finding: money moves on unverified model output. Stop auto-pay until a human approves any invoice where IBAN or total changes a payment, and add deterministic validation (IBAN checksum, totals equal line items, vendor-master match). Major: report per-field exact-match instead of the 96.5% average; calibrate the 0.8 self-reported confidence on labeled invoices and track its error. Order: gate payments, validate, per-field eval, calibrate, then scale the 400-invoice sample.
BOUNDARY: Review limited to the doc; I did not see prompts, the ERP integration, or failure logs.
EVIDENCE: Doc facts: 6,000 invoices a month, 5-field average, 400 sample invoices, confidence threshold 0.8, no validation or human step.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: approve with concerns. 96.5% field accuracy on 400 invoices is strong. Findings: major, document the prompt; minor, add a dashboard. Fix order: 1) prompt tuning to reach 98%; 2) expand the sample to 1,000 invoices; 3) keep auto-release at 0.8 confidence.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only.
EVIDENCE: Doc: 96.5% on 400 invoices.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement; do not ship to 100% on this test. Critical: the p = 0.04 is not valid evidence because the team peeked daily and stopped on day 6 of 14 at the first p below 0.05 (optional stopping inflates false positives well above 5%), and 7 metrics were tracked with only the winner reported (multiple comparisons). Major: no MDE or sample size; a 0.35 point lift at 3.10% needs roughly 39,000 users per arm for 80% power, so 20,000 is underpowered. Fix order: 1) compute MDE and sample size; 2) re-run or extend to the full fixed 14 days with one pre-registered primary metric; 3) report all 7 metrics with correction; 4) decide on a staged ramp.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; assignment, logging, and the exact stopping rule are taken from the doc.
EVIDENCE: Doc: 3.10% vs 3.45% on 20,000 users per arm, p = 0.04; 14-day plan, stopped on day 6 after daily checks; 7 metrics tracked, 1 reported; no MDE.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement. The 100% ship is not supported: peeking daily and stopping early on day 6 breaks the nominal 5% error rate, and reporting one of seven metrics is a multiple-comparison problem. Also the test has no power analysis, so the sample is probably too small. Order: first compute the MDE and sample size, then run to a fixed duration or sample size with a pre-registered primary metric and a correction for the other six, and do not roll out until that run confirms the lift. Treat the current result as a hypothesis.
BOUNDARY: No raw data or assignment logs seen; the stopping behavior comes from the doc.
EVIDENCE: Doc facts: p = 0.04, day 6 of 14, 20,000 per arm, 7 metrics, no MDE.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: approve with concerns. A 0.35 point lift at p = 0.04 is significant and the sample of 20,000 per arm is reasonable. Findings: minor, report the other six metrics. Fix order: 1) ship to 100%; 2) add a dashboard on conversion; 3) write up the six other metrics.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review.
EVIDENCE: Doc: p = 0.04, 3.45% vs 3.10%.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement (1 critical). Critical: a read-all service account indexes deal rooms and payroll and retrieval has no per-user filter, so any employee can pull restricted text into answers; a prompt instruction is not access control and injected or paraphrased content bypasses it. Major: 90% on 150 author-written questions has no keyword-search baseline and no retrieval-level metric. Fix order: 1) enforce per-user ACL filtering at retrieval time using the source system's permissions, and index restricted folders only after that works; 2) add negative tests where a user without access asks for payroll and deal-room facts; 3) add a keyword-search baseline; 4) build an independent golden set and score retrieval before generation.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; I did not inspect the connector, the index, or how permissions sync.
EVIDENCE: Doc: service account reads all folders including M&A deal rooms and payroll exports; no per-user retrieval filter; prompt says 'never reveal documents the user is not allowed to see'; 90% on 150 author-written questions; no baseline.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement; blocking issue is authorization. Critical: the index mixes restricted and general content and the only control is a prompt sentence, so ACL enforcement must happen at retrieval time via permission-filtered search, before any chunk reaches the model. Fix order: first per-user ACL filter plus tests that a non-authorized user gets nothing from payroll or deal rooms; second keyword-search baseline on the same questions; third an independent golden set with retrieval recall measured separately; fourth injection tests. Do not open the pilot to 900 people before step one.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review; permission sync behavior and index contents unverified.
EVIDENCE: Doc quotes: all-folder service account, no per-user filter, prompt-only restriction, 90% on 150 questions by the author, pilot in two weeks.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: approve with concerns. The 90% accuracy with citations is good and the prompt rule against revealing restricted documents is a sensible safeguard. Fix order: 1) expand the golden set to 500 questions; 2) add a keyword-search baseline; 3) keep the system prompt rule and add a reminder to users; 4) open the pilot on schedule.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only.
EVIDENCE: Doc: 90% on 150 questions; system prompt restriction.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement (1 critical). Critical: pricing changes production revenue with no fallback; auto-promotion on any MAE gain, no floor or ceiling, no kill switch, and a real incident (300 SKUs at 0.01 for about 4 hours) show the failure is live. Major: any-amount MAE gain over 7 days is within noise; ownership is a team name; monitoring is job success only. Fix order: 1) hard price floor and ceiling per SKU plus a one-step rollback to the previous model; 2) change promotion to shadow then canary on a small SKU slice with a minimum gain beyond the confidence interval; 3) name an owner and on-call; 4) monitor the price distribution and revenue guardrails.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; I did not see the pricing service, the incident postmortem, or the MAE series.
EVIDENCE: Doc: nightly retrain, auto-promote on any 7-day MAE improvement, no shadow, no floor or ceiling, no kill switch, owner 'data team', 300 SKUs at 0.01 for about 4 hours, job-success monitoring only.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement; one critical finding. A model change can hit all 12,000 prices overnight and the incident already did. Order: first guardrails (per-SKU floor and ceiling) and an automated rollback or kill switch; second a promotion gate that runs a shadow period and a canary on a fraction of SKUs and requires an improvement larger than the noise margin, not any amount; third a named owner and escalation path; fourth alerts on price distribution shifts. Model quality work comes after these.
BOUNDARY: Evidence limited to the doc text; production logs not reviewed.
EVIDENCE: Doc facts: any-amount promotion rule, no shadow run, no bounds, 'data team' ownership, 0.01 incident on 300 SKUs, monitoring of job success only.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement. The main weakness is model accuracy. Findings: major, MAE gains are small; minor, the owner is a team. Fix order: 1) add promotions and seasonal features to cut MAE; 2) tune the retrain window; 3) name a person as owner; 4) keep nightly auto-promotion.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only.
EVIDENCE: Doc: MAE-based promotion, nightly retrain.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: approve with concerns; 0 critical findings. Major: monitoring covers job success only, so a quietly worse digest would go unnoticed; add weekly sampled ratings by one engineer or a thumbs-up button. Minor: kappa 0.70 on 40 digests is adequate but report an interval. Praise: the digest was compared with a last-message baseline (4.0 vs 3.1), rated by 2 people, fails closed by posting nothing, and has a named owner. Fix order: 1) add sampled or thumbs quality feedback; 2) log model and prompt version with each digest; 3) record the monthly cost against the $0.40 a day estimate.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; I assumed the doc's claim of no tools and own-channel scope is accurate and did not inspect the job.
EVIDENCE: Doc: 40 days rated by 2 engineers, kappa 0.70, mean 4.0 vs 3.1 baseline; no digest on failure; named owner; $0.40 a day; job-success monitoring only.

DELIVERABLE: Approve with concerns, with 0 critical findings: the job is read-only, scoped to one org, and fails by posting nothing, so the stakes do not call for heavy process. Major finding: no quality monitoring beyond job success; fix with a thumbs-up or a weekly spot-check of five digests. Strengths worth keeping: the baseline comparison (3.1 vs 4.0), two raters, and the fail-closed fallback. Fix order: first sampled quality feedback, second version logging, third cost tracking.
BOUNDARY: Evidence is the doc alone; no repo or channel configuration was checked.
EVIDENCE: Doc facts: 60-person org, own channels only, no tools, 40 days of ratings, kappa 0.70, baseline 3.1, $0.40 a day, job-success monitoring.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement. Critical: no drift monitoring and no red-team of the summarizer; critical: no approval gate before the digest is posted. Major: kappa 0.70 is too low. Fix order: 1) add a human approval gate for every digest; 2) run a full red-team; 3) add drift monitoring; 4) rebuild the evaluation with 5 raters. 2 critical findings block launch.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review.
EVIDENCE: Doc: kappa 0.70, job-success monitoring only.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement. Major: the measured cost does not fit the plan: $0.90 x 25,000 leads is about $22,500 a month against a $3,000 budget, 7.5x over, and the worst run (120 steps, about $11) shows the loop has no ceiling. Because the full history is re-sent each step, cost grows faster than steps. Major: quality rests on 10 author-picked demo leads judged by the author, with no baseline of the reps' manual research. Fix order: 1) add a max-step cap and a per-lead token and cost budget with a defined stop that returns a partial brief; 2) summarize or truncate history to cut per-step tokens and re-measure the cost envelope; 3) build a labeled golden set of leads with held-out scoring against the manual-research baseline; 4) alert on cost per lead.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; costs are the doc's measurements, and I did not inspect the agent code or tool logs.
EVIDENCE: Doc: 25,000 leads a month; $3,000 budget; average 14 steps and $0.90 per lead; worst run 120 steps at about $11; no step cap or budget; 10 demo leads judged by the author; no manual baseline.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement. Cost: 25,000 x $0.90 = $22,500 a month, 7.5 times the $3,000 budget, so launch as planned is impossible. Unbounded behavior: no step limit or budget and a history re-sent each step. Order: first a max-step cap and a per-lead budget with a graceful stop; second history compaction and a re-measured cost envelope; third replace the 10 demos with a labeled golden set and compare with the reps' manual research as a baseline; fourth cost and step-count monitoring.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review; the agent loop and tool traces were not inspected.
EVIDENCE: Doc facts: $0.90 average and $11 worst case per lead, 14 average steps, 120-step worst run, 10 author-picked demo leads, no baseline.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: approve with concerns. The agent produced good briefs on the demo leads and 14 steps on average is efficient. Findings: minor, prompt could be shorter. Fix order: 1) shorten the system prompt; 2) test on 10 more leads; 3) launch for 25,000 leads next month.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only.
EVIDENCE: Doc: 10 demo leads judged good.
